title: ECM Critical Internal Failure
shortDescription: Cummins ECM has a critical internal fault — reflash or replacement required.
fullDescription:
Cummins SPN 111 FMI 12 (Fault Code 111 on classic display) indicates the Cummins engine control module has detected a critical internal failure. Applies across ISB, ISC, ISL, ISX platforms.

Causes: voltage spike damage (jump-starting reversed, welding without disconnect), lightning, end-of-life, water intrusion. The ECM may still start the engine but will run in a limp/default mode.

Diagnosis is dealer-level. Cummins INSITE can attempt a reflash. If unsuccessful, replacement is required — ECM costs $1,500-$3,000 plus labor and programming.

fixSteps.title: Check power/ground
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm ECM power > 12.4V at rest. Inspect all grounds for tightness and corrosion.

fixSteps.title: Reflash at dealer
fixSteps.instruction: Cummins dealer with INSITE attempts ECM reflash with current calibration.

fixSteps.title: Replace ECM
fixSteps.instruction: If reflash fails, replace ECM and program with VIN, parameters, fuel map.

videoSearchQuery: Cummins fault code 111 ECM internal failure reflash

faq.a: Always — welding induces voltage spikes that fry ECMs.
Must be programmed by Cummins with correct cal and injector trims.

title: Engine Crankshaft Speed High (Overspeed)
shortDescription: Crankshaft RPM exceeded maximum — overrev event or sensor error.
fullDescription:
Cummins Fault 234 indicates engine RPM exceeded the maximum allowable — typically 2300-2400 RPM depending on the ISX/ISL configuration. Common during aggressive downshifts or downhill overrun in manual transmissions.

A single event from downshifting is not serious but should be noted. Repeated events may indicate a runaway risk — oil-fed runaway from turbo seal failure or crankcase oil ingestion is a catastrophic concern.

Emergency runaway shutdown: block air intake with jacket or heavy floor mat. Diesel needs air to run.

fixSteps.title: Review event
fixSteps.instruction: Pull freeze frame via INSITE — confirms if RPM spike matched coast/downshift or unexplained acceleration.

fixSteps.title: Turbo/CCV check
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect turbo shaft play and CCV breather for oil mist. Indicates oil ingestion risk.

fixSteps.title: Sensor check
fixSteps.instruction: If no oil issue, inspect crank sensor and tone wheel for damage.

faq.a: Block intake. Diesel has no spark — cutting air stops combustion.
Usually if clearly a downshift event — monitor for repeats.

title: Engine Timing Reference Signal Error
shortDescription: Crank/cam timing correlation error — sensor or tone wheel fault.
fullDescription:
Cummins fault 637 indicates the ECM detects a timing error between crank and cam signals. FMI 8 = abnormal frequency/pattern.

Causes: failed cam or crank sensor, damaged tone wheel teeth, or metal debris on sensor tip. On ISX/X15, also commonly caused by timing gear wear at high mileage.

Engine may start but run rough or not start at all. Diagnose both sensors and verify tone wheel integrity before condemning internal components.

causes.cause: Failed crank or cam position sensor

fixSteps.title: Clean sensors
fixSteps.instruction: Remove crank and cam sensors. Wipe metallic debris. Re-install with correct torque.

fixSteps.title: Scope test
fixSteps.instruction: With scope, check signal pattern of both sensors during cranking.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor or inspect tone wheel
fixSteps.instruction: If sensor replacement doesn't clear, dealer inspects tone wheel for damage.

videoSearchQuery: Cummins ISX fault 115 cam crank timing SPN 637

faq.q: Can I start with just crank sensor?
faq.a: Some Cummins strategies start on crank alone — rough idle but runs.
Some is expected — clean at each service.

title: Oil Change Interval Expired
shortDescription: Service reminder — engine oil and filter due for change.
fullDescription:
Cummins SPN 1378 is a service reminder when the algorithm-based oil change interval has been reached. Based on fuel burn, idle hours, and operational severity factors. Not a fault, but a maintenance prompt.

Failing to service causes oil degradation — acids, particulates, and fuel dilution accelerate bearing wear. Skipped services shorten Cummins engine life substantially.

Reset interval via INSITE or dealer after service.

fixSteps.title: Change oil and filter
fixSteps.instruction: Drain and replace oil with correct spec (CK-4 15W-40 typical for ISX). Replace full-flow and bypass filters.

fixSteps.title: Reset interval
fixSteps.instruction: With INSITE, reset oil change interval counter. Dash reminder clears.

whenToCallPro: If INSITE not available for reset.
videoSearchQuery: Cummins oil change reset SPN 1378 fault 649

faq.a: Eventually triggers power derate — service on time.

title: VGT Turbo Actuator Stuck
shortDescription: Variable geometry turbo actuator not moving — stuck with soot or mechanical failure.
fullDescription:
SPN 2556 FMI 7 on Cummins ISX/X15 engines indicates the VGT actuator is not moving to commanded position. Most common cause: carbon buildup around the vane linkage. Running ISX under light load accumulates carbon rapidly.

Holset VGT actuators (smart, electronic) on ISX can also fail electronically. Calibration via INSITE sometimes frees lightly stuck vanes. Severe cases need turbo removal for solvent soak or replacement.

New ISX VGT turbo is $3,500-$5,500. Actuator alone is ~$1,500 if separately available.

fixSteps.title: Calibration attempt
fixSteps.instruction: Run VGT calibration in INSITE — cycles actuator several times, may free light carbon.

fixSteps.title: Turbo service
fixSteps.instruction: Remove turbo, soak cold side in solvent, work vanes free by hand. Reassemble and recalibrate.

fixSteps.title: Replace turbo
fixSteps.instruction: If vanes cannot be freed, replace VGT assembly. Recalibrate via INSITE.

videoSearchQuery: Cummins ISX VGT stuck SPN 2556 Holset clean

faq.a: Yes — first step, often frees light carbon.
Avoid long idle, run highway miles weekly.

title: Aftertreatment NOx Bank 1 Low
shortDescription: Bank 1 (inlet) NOx reading lower than expected.
fullDescription:
SPN 4335 FMI 18 on Cummins X15/ISX monitors inlet (engine-out) NOx. FMI 18 = data valid but below expected. Often means inlet NOx sensor is drifting low with age, or EGR is flowing more than expected (stuck open).

Drifting NOx sensors are #1 cause. Replace in pairs with outlet sensor for matched aging. Clear code and perform drive cycle to learn new sensor.

fixSteps.title: Check EGR
fixSteps.instruction: Command EGR 0% via INSITE at idle. If flow still suspected, pull EGR valve and inspect.

fixSteps.title: Inspect exhaust seals
fixSteps.instruction: Check V-band clamps upstream of inlet NOx sensor for leaks.

fixSteps.title: Replace NOx sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap inlet (and outlet for matched pair) NOx sensor.

videoSearchQuery: Cummins X15 SPN 4335 inlet NOx sensor

faq.a: Yes — match aging prevents chasing SCR codes.
Only if secondary symptoms suggest — otherwise sensor age is most common.

title: Aftertreatment NOx Bank 2 (Outlet) Low
shortDescription: Outlet NOx reading lower than model expects — sensor or SCR issue.
fullDescription:
SPN 4355 FMI 18 on Cummins X15/ISX represents outlet (post-SCR) NOx lower than expected based on model. Could be normal if SCR is working well, but combined with low inlet reading, both sensors may be drifting.

Diagnose: if inlet is normal but outlet reads zero at all conditions, outlet sensor is drifted low. Replace with OEM Cummins sensor — $700-$900.

SCR catalyst replacement is rare cause — only if sensors both check out and catalyst is damaged.

fixSteps.title: Compare sensors
fixSteps.instruction: With INSITE, monitor both NOx sensors at steady highway cruise. Outlet near 0 consistently = drift.

fixSteps.title: Replace outlet NOx
fixSteps.instruction: Cool engine. 22mm NOx socket. Anti-seize on threads only, never on sensing tip.

videoSearchQuery: Cummins X15 outlet NOx SPN 4355 replace

title: Aftertreatment SCR Inducement Active
shortDescription: EPA inducement in progress — fix root cause before 5 mph derate.
fullDescription:
Cummins SPN 5246 FMI 31 indicates the SCR inducement counter is active — a primary fault (DEF empty, quality, NOx, dosing, etc.) has not been resolved. EPA-mandated derate cascade will engage.

Companion code only — find and fix the root cause. Common primaries: SPN 3610 (DEF empty), SPN 3364 (DEF quality), SPN 4364 (SCR efficiency), SPN 4094 (DEF pressure).

Inducement resets automatically after primary clears + drive cycle.

fixSteps.title: Scan all codes
fixSteps.instruction: INSITE full code pull to identify primary SCR fault.

fixSteps.title: Fix primary
fixSteps.instruction: Address per primary SPN procedure (DEF refill, flush, sensor replace, etc.).

fixSteps.title: Drive cycle reset
fixSteps.instruction: After fix, drive cycle normalizes inducement. Dealer can force reset if needed.

faq.a: Typically 20-40 hours of operation with primary fault.

title: Water in Fuel — Severe
shortDescription: Water detected in fuel/water separator — drain immediately to prevent injector damage.
fullDescription:
Cummins fault 418 / SPN 97 FMI 0 indicates a significant amount of water has accumulated in the fuel/water separator. Continued operation risks destroying high-pressure common rail injectors (30,000+ PSI operating pressure) — repair cost $5,000+.

ISB, ISL, ISX platforms all use a primary fuel/water separator with a drain valve. Open drain, collect water until pure diesel flows. Modern ISX filter housings have a priming pump to restore flow.

If water keeps coming back, tank contamination is likely — may need fuel polishing or tank pumpout.

fixSteps.title: Drain separator
fixSteps.instruction: Open drain at bottom of separator bowl into a clear container. Close when pure diesel flows.

fixSteps.title: Prime and test
fixSteps.instruction: Use priming pump. Start engine, clear code with INSITE or reset.

fixSteps.title: Investigate if repeats
fixSteps.instruction: If water returns quickly, test tank fuel sample and check cap seal.

videoSearchQuery: Cummins water in fuel drain SPN 97 fault 418

faq.a: 30,000 PSI water pulse = $5,000+ injector failure. Drain now.
Drain at every fuel filter change, weekly in humid climates.

title: Fuel Rail Pressure Below Expected
shortDescription: Common rail fuel pressure low — supply, pump, or sensor fault.
fullDescription:
Cummins SPN 157 FMI 4 / Fault 449 on ISX/X15/ISL indicates common rail pressure is below what the ECM commands. Rail operates at 25,000-32,000 PSI during peak injection.

SAFETY: Common rail fuel at this pressure can inject through skin invisibly, causing serious injection injuries. Wait 10+ minutes after shutdown before any rail work. Never loosen fittings with engine running.

Check supply pressure (SPN 94) first — starving supply is cheap to fix. Then sensor. Then pump ($3,500-$5,000).

fixSteps.title: Change fuel filters
fixSteps.instruction: Replace primary and secondary filters. Prime system.

fixSteps.title: Measure supply pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Mechanical gauge at HPFP inlet — should be 60-90 PSI. Below = lift pump or filter issue.

fixSteps.title: Return flow test / HPFP
fixSteps.instruction: Dealer — return flow at each injector. HPFP replacement if out of spec.

videoSearchQuery: Cummins ISX fault 449 rail pressure SPN 157

faq.a: Yes, amputation risk. Wait times and PPE essential.
Fuel filters $50 always precede $5,000 HPFP diagnosis.

title: Coolant Temp High — Moderate
shortDescription: Coolant temperature above normal — power derate engaged.
fullDescription:
Cummins fault 146 / SPN 110 FMI 16 indicates coolant temp between warning and shutdown thresholds. ECM derates power to protect engine from head gasket failure.

Check coolant level, radiator fins, fan clutch. ISX/X15 have heavy thermal load — cooling system must be clean.

Overtemp ISX easily costs $15,000+ in internal damage if ignored.

fixSteps.title: Safe cooldown
fixSteps.instruction: Idle 2-3 min, shut down, wait 30+ min before opening cap.

fixSteps.title: Inspect and top off
fixSteps.instruction: Check level, rinse fins, inspect for external leaks.

fixSteps.title: Fan and combustion test
fixSteps.instruction: Command fan via INSITE. Combustion gas test if coolant disappears internally.

faq.a: Should audibly lock above 210°F — or use INSITE to command.

title: DPF Pressure Very High — Service Required
shortDescription: DPF delta pressure at severe threshold — cannot regen, dealer service needed.
fullDescription:
Cummins fault 1921 indicates the DPF differential pressure is at the severe threshold — regen cannot safely complete. 5 mph derate active.

Requires dealer forced regen via INSITE or DPF removal for off-vehicle thermal/pneumatic cleaning. Ash load from oil burn may also mandate service cleaning every 200,000-300,000 miles.

Replacement DPF $4,500+ if substrate cracked from prior thermal event.

fixSteps.title: Tow to dealer
fixSteps.instruction: 5 mph derate too slow for road travel — tow to Cummins dealer.

fixSteps.title: Forced regen or clean
fixSteps.instruction: Dealer attempts INSITE forced regen. If fails, DPF removed for thermal service.

fixSteps.title: Replace if substrate damaged
fixSteps.instruction: New DPF assembly if substrate cracked.

videoSearchQuery: Cummins fault 1921 DPF severe forced regen

faq.a: Regular highway miles, scheduled DPF cleaning intervals.
Use EPA-approved replacements — illegal if not certified.

title: DEF Tank Level Low Warning
shortDescription: DEF tank approaching empty — refill soon.
fullDescription:
Cummins SPN 3610 FMI 18 is the first-level low DEF warning on ISX/X15 and ISB/ISL trucks. Amber lamp illuminates, no derate yet — driver has time to refill before inducement.

Topping off with API-certified DEF at any truck stop resolves the code. Ignoring progresses through warning levels to the 5 mph limp-home.

Monitor tank cap — loose cap lets rain in, contaminating DEF.

causes.cause: DEF consumption higher than fill schedule

fixSteps.title: Refill DEF
fixSteps.instruction: Add API-certified DEF to 50%+ tank. Code clears on next drive cycle.

faq.a: ISX uses ~2-3% of diesel gallons in DEF.
API-certified only — look for API Diesel Exhaust Fluid mark.

title: DPF Soot High — Active Regen Needed
shortDescription: Soot above moderate threshold — complete regen required now.
fullDescription:
Cummins SPN 3719 FMI 16 / fault 1922 indicates DPF soot load in the moderate warning range. Stationary or parked regen should clear it. If allowed to escalate, 5 mph derate follows.

On Cummins ISX/X15 with PACCAR or Kenworth/Peterbilt chassis, parked regen is initiated from dash switch. 30-45 minutes in a safe open area.

Frequent regen needs indicate duty cycle issue or failing dosing system.

fixSteps.title: Parked regen
fixSteps.instruction: Safe location, brake set, neutral, initiate regen. 30-45 min.

fixSteps.title: Highway drive
fixSteps.instruction: Follow with 30+ min highway cruise to establish passive regen.

title: SCR Conversion Efficiency Low
shortDescription: SCR converting below EPA threshold — early warning before derate.
fullDescription:
Cummins SPN 4364 FMI 17 on ISX/X15 indicates NOx conversion across the SCR catalyst is below expected — least severe. Repair now before FMI 18 (derate) follows.

Troubleshoot in order: NOx sensors (most common), DEF dosing rate, DEF quality, exhaust leaks, catalyst condition.

NOx sensor kits (both inlet + outlet) are the fastest-fix starting point for 4364 codes.

fixSteps.title: Read NOx live
fixSteps.instruction: Steady cruise monitor both NOx — unrealistic low outlet or equal inlet/outlet = sensor issue.

fixSteps.title: Check dosing
fixSteps.instruction: Dosing test via INSITE. Low flow = filter or doser issue.

videoSearchQuery: Cummins X15 SPN 4364 FMI 17 SCR efficiency

faq.a: Yes — FMI 17 is warning, FMI 18 starts inducement.

title: Ammonia Slip / SCR Over-Dosing
shortDescription: Excess ammonia slipping past SCR — overdose or low catalyst activity.
fullDescription:
On some Cummins ISX/X15 configurations, SPN 5246 FMI 15 indicates ammonia slip detected at outlet — SCR dosing rate exceeds catalyst ability to convert, so unreacted ammonia (from DEF breakdown) passes through.

Causes: aged SCR catalyst losing activity, doser over-spraying (stuck), or catalyst face crystallized from past over-dosing.

Dealer-level SCR efficiency diagnosis usually required.

fixSteps.title: Doser test
fixSteps.instruction: Run dosing test via INSITE. Measure ml/min and compare to spec.

fixSteps.title: SCR thermal service
fixSteps.instruction: Dealer thermal bake removes urea crystals from catalyst face.

videoSearchQuery: Cummins X15 ammonia slip SPN 5246 SCR

faq.a: Never — indicates SCR or doser issue.
Diagnose first — doser is cheaper to rule out.

title: Fuel Delivery Pressure Low
shortDescription: Low-side fuel supply pressure below spec — filter, lift pump, or suction air leak.
fullDescription:
Cummins SPN 94 FMI 18 / Fault 559 indicates low-pressure fuel supply to the HPFP is below spec (typically 50-80 PSI). Low supply starves HPFP, causes cavitation, risks HPFP metal contamination of the rail ($7,000+ failure).

Most common: plugged secondary filter. Change filters, prime, retest. If pressure still low, suspect lift pump or suction-side air leak.

Cummins Fleetguard filters recommended for correct micron rating and efficiency.

fixSteps.title: Change filters
fixSteps.instruction: Primary + secondary Fleetguard filters. Prime system.

fixSteps.title: Measure pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Mechanical gauge at HPFP inlet — 50-80 PSI expected.

fixSteps.title: Clear bubble test
fixSteps.instruction: Clear hose inline — bubbles indicate suction leak.

videoSearchQuery: Cummins ISX fault 559 low fuel pressure SPN 94

faq.a: Fleetguard highly recommended — wrong micron = injector damage.
Supply pressure in spec + clean fuel = long HPFP life.

title: Boost Pressure Low
shortDescription: Charge air pressure below commanded — leak, VGT, or CAC fault.
fullDescription:
Cummins SPN 102 FMI 18 / Fault 2449 on ISX/X15 indicates intake boost is below commanded value. Most commonly a CAC (charge air cooler) leak — boot or clamp.

Smoke-test charge air system first. Any leak drops boost and fuel economy. VGT soot fouling is next most common. On high-mileage ISX, consider VGT service at 500,000+ miles.

fixSteps.title: Smoke test
fixSteps.instruction: Pressurize CAC system, watch for leaks.

fixSteps.title: Repair leak
fixSteps.instruction: Tighten clamps, replace boots or CAC.

fixSteps.title: VGT test
fixSteps.instruction: INSITE command 0-100%, watch response. Service if sticking.

videoSearchQuery: Cummins ISX boost leak SPN 102 fault 2449

faq.a: Smoke catches tiny leaks soap misses.
End tank splits at 500,000+ miles on ISX trucks.
